THOUGHT: A postmenopausal woman with a year of severe vulvar pruritus and dyspareunia, objective findings of thin, white plaque-like lesions with labial atrophy and clitoral retraction and pale wrinkled perianal skin are highly suggestive of a chronic vulvar dermatosis. The biopsy shows hyperkeratosis, epidermal thinning with loss of rete ridges and sclerosis of the dermis — histopathologic features classic for lichen sclerosus. Other possibilities (atrophic vaginitis from estrogen deficiency, lichen planus, lichen simplex chronicus, vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia) are less likely given the clinical distribution, the sclerotic dermal change on biopsy, and lack of epithelial atypia or erosive/interface changes. These clinical and histologic findings together point to vulvar lichen sclerosus.

DIAGNOSIS: Vulvar lichen sclerosus
